svg.title: Summation polynomials and Weil restriction
svg.desc: The difficult task is finding admissible solutions; polynomial identities alone do not establish a fast solver.
svg.text: The difficult task is finding admissible solutions; polynomial identities alone do not establish a fast solver.
Assume characteristic >3 for the displayed short model. More general factor bases impose their own coordinate constraints.
Roots encode geometric lifts; verify field membership and the signed group relation.
CHOOSE A BASIS 1, ω, …, ωᵈ⁻¹ OF K OVER 𝔽q
Dimension heuristic: m−d. At m=d the system is generically zero-dimensional only if these constraints are independent.
Gaudry’s heuristic regime: a suitable nondegenerate
factor base and controlled decomposition cost.
The canonical system collapses to one base-field equation.
A nonrational x-line changes this system and must be analyzed.
A summation-polynomial zero is not yet a verified relation in the intended group. Solver and independence assumptions are substantive.
